Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

simtte (development version)

  • The blog post Driving a hazard from a PK/PD ODE system in simtte is now an article on the package website.

simtte 2.0.0

A major release. It adds in-solver time-to-event simulation, censoring and visit schedules. It also corrects sim_tte() behaviours that change its results or checks compared with CRAN 1.0.2; see “Breaking changes”.

Breaking changes

  • sim_tte() uses time as the output grid. Event times (sim_time) change whenever time is finer than 1, for example by a mean of 16.6% for the README Weibull example. Pass time = seq(0, end, by = 1) to reproduce the 1.0.2 grid. The default of time is now seq(0, 100, by = 1), the same effective resolution as before.
  • sim_tte() computes the Weibull survival probability in closed form, S(t) = exp(-exp(mu + lp) * t^shape). Results for shape != 1 change at small times; 1.0.2 was off by up to 0.16 for shape < 1.
  • sim_tte() applies each M-spline hazard value over the interval that follows its time point (nocb = FALSE), so M-spline survival trajectories and event times change. See ?sim_tte, “M-spline hazard carry convention”.
  • sim_tte(), explore_pi_tq_surv() and sim_tte_ode() raise an error naming the argument if ... supplies tgrid, obsonly, nocb, carry_out or data, which would break the output-grid contract. Remove the argument.
  • sim_tte() rejects an M-spline end_time outside min(time) <= end_time <= max(time), and rejects non-finite or mismatched basis, coefs or basehaz, a negative resulting hazard, and duplicate time values with conflicting hazards.

New features

  • add_censoring() applies independent right censoring to any events data frame from sim_tte_ode(), sim_tte() or sim_tte_df(). It draws censoring times from an exponential, Weibull, uniform, lognormal, gamma or user-supplied distribution, updates sim_time and sim_status, and records the outcome in a new sim_reason column ("event", "censored" or "administrative"). sim_tte_ode() also takes censoring, so one seed reproduces the whole simulation. Informative (dependent) censoring is not available.
  • add_interval_censoring() maps events onto a visit schedule, adding sim_time_left and sim_time_right columns for (L, R] intervals and (L, Inf) for subjects censored event-free. The columns feed survival::Surv(type = "interval2") after converting Inf to NA; an event with sim_time_left == 0 is left-censored. sim_tte_ode() also takes visits, applied after any censoring.
  • censoring_rate_for() solves for the censoring-distribution parameter that gives a target censoring fraction from the event times of an uncensored run.
  • draw_censoring_times(spec, n, seed = NULL) draws directly from an add_censoring() distribution spec, with no events data frame.
  • sim_tte() and sim_tte_df() gain event_time_method. "grid" (the default) keeps the first reported time at which survival reaches the uniform draw. "log_survival" interpolates the cumulative hazard between the two surrounding reported times: exact for the M-spline model and an approximation that improves with a finer grid for continuously varying hazards. Event versus censored classification is identical for the same seed.
  • sim_tte() takes a time-varying lp_data: a per-subject or population-level log hazard ratio trajectory, carried forward between supplied time points.
  • sim_tte_ode() simulates joint PK/PD and time-to-event data with in-solver event detection. Survival is one more ODE compartment (dxdt_p11 = -p11 * HAZ), and each event time is located during integration, where p11 first falls to or below a per-subject uniform draw. Built-in models are "exponential", "weibull", "gompertz" and "mspline" (quadratic M-spline hazard with 3, 5 or 7 interior knots).
  • sim_tte_ode() includes six PK/PD-linked hazard models built on unedited mrgsolve::modlib() backbones: "pk_hazard" (concentration-driven), "irm1_hazard" to "irm4_hazard" (response-driven) and "tmdd_hazard" (target-mediated drug disposition). Dosing is ordinary mrgsolve event data passed as data. A data frame whose unique IDs do not match the resolved subject count errors, naming both numbers.
  • sim_tte_ode() takes covariates and beta (optionally formula) for a log-linear linear predictor, lp(t) = sum_k beta_k * X_k(t). formula (for example ~ age + arm) builds the design matrix with stats::model.matrix(), so factors, interactions and terms such as I(age^2) or splines::ns(weight, 3) work. covariates can be baseline (one row per subject) or time-varying. An implied intercept is dropped with a message, as in survival::coxph(). A baseline frame with one row and no ID applies to every subject; with several rows it sets the subject count.
  • sim_tte_ode() takes omega for log-normal between-subject variability on a model’s structural PK/PD parameters, applied through per-subject idata, so no $OMEGA block is needed. A model that declares its own $OMEGA uses mrgsolve::omat() instead; omega or sigma on a model with no matching block explains this rather than surfacing the mrgsolve error.
  • sim_tte_ode_models() lists the built-in model names accepted by sim_tte_ode(model = ) with each model’s valid omega targets.
  • simtte_example_model() and simtte_example_models() load and list two bundled, editable mrgsolve models for use with sim_tte_df().
  • simtte_model_cache() reports where compiled models are stored (under tempdir() by default). Set options(simtte.cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("simtte", "cache")) to keep them across sessions.
  • simtte_model_cache_clear(all = FALSE) removes compiled models for the current R, simtte and mrgsolve versions, or for every version with all = TRUE. It only removes directories simtte created.
  • simtte_prepare_model(model, ...) builds (or reuses) and loads a model once so sim_tte_ode() never rebuilds it. Call it once per parallel::makePSOCKcluster() worker, then pass the same model to later sim_tte_ode() calls. It rebuilds a tte_model() result from its stored code in a fresh process, so a saved object works in a separate R process. For "mspline" it takes knots; coefs and boundary_knots error. See ?sim_tte_ode, “Parallel simulation”.
  • thin_visits(visits, ...) drops visits with probability p_miss and starts dropout with probability p_dropout. It reads no outcome, so it never makes a schedule informative. Run it before add_interval_censoring().
  • tte_model() converts your own mrgsolve PK/PD model for sim_tte_ode(), from code, a file path or a compiled model. It adds the survival compartment without editing your $ODE/$DES and reproduces the six built-in hazard models from their modlib() backbones.
  • visit_schedule() builds a per-subject schedule with fixed spacing and jitter. jitter_dist = "normal" is truncated at +/- jitter_trunc * jitter (default jitter_trunc = 2), and a jitter large enough to reorder visits is an error.
  • visit_schedule_informative(visits, events, ...) makes attendance react to the simulated event time. miss_near_event raises the chance of missing a visit shortly before an event, and extra_visit_after_event adds a visit after it. miss_near_event$p and p_miss_base combine as competing risks, 1 - (1 - p_miss_base) * (1 - p). The schedule is informative by construction, and every call says so with a message().

Minor improvements and fixes

  • Help pages link related functions and say why they go together, ?simtte gains a “Which functions go together” section, and the model, events and name arguments say where their values come from.
  • sim_tte() accepts end_time = 0; every subject is censored at 0.
  • sim_tte_df() clamps survival values within 1e-8 of [0, 1] to 0 or 1 before checking monotonicity. Values further outside still error.
  • sim_tte_df() and sim_tte_ode() document that a fixed seed reproduces results for a fixed row order of the input.

simtte 1.0.2

CRAN release: 2026-07-31

  • Fixed time-column position bug in sim_tte_df(): time is now resolved by column name, not position.
  • Preserved original subject IDs in output (no longer renumbered).
  • Corrected .get_tte() to use the conventional <= U inverse-transform boundary rule.
  • Added optional time_var argument to sim_tte_df().
  • Changed package Title to “Simulate Bespoke Time-to-Event Models Using ODEs” and rewrote the Description to frame simtte around bespoke ODE-based time-to-event models (built-in Weibull/M-spline hazards plus fully custom mrgsolve ODE systems), rather than Weibull and spline models specifically.

simtte 1.0.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-11

  • Fixed issues from CRAN review:
    • Added \value tag to pipe.Rd documenting the return value of the pipe operator.
    • Reduced example run times and unwrapped short examples from \donttest{} so they run during automated checks; examples now execute in under 5 seconds.

simtte 1.0.0

  • Initial CRAN release.
  • Simulate time-to-event datasets using Weibull and M-spline baseline hazard models.
  • Inverse transform sampling from cumulative hazard functions via mrgsolve ODE solver.
  • Exported functions: sim_tte(), sim_tte_df(), explore_pi_tq_surv().
  • Includes example M-spline dataset (ms_data).
  • Two vignettes: “Getting Started” and “Advanced Simulation Scenarios”.
